mcq.s: In which year did Muhammad bin Qasim conquer Sindh?
mcq.x: The Arab general Muhammad bin Qasim defeated and killed Raja Dahir and conquered Sindh in 712 A.D., the first successful Muslim invasion of India.

mcq.s: The first Muslim invader of India was:
mcq.x: The Arab Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 712 A.D., long before the Ghaznavid and Ghurid invasions.

mcq.s: The first Muslim invaders of India were:
mcq.x: The Arabs under Muhammad bin Qasim invaded and conquered Sindh in 712 A.D., before the Ghaznavids and the Ghurids.

mcq.s: Muhammad bin Qasim, the conqueror of Sindh, was a/an:
mcq.x: Muhammad bin Qasim was an Arab general, sent by Al-Hajjaj (governor of Iraq) under the Umayyad Caliph al-Walid; he conquered Sindh in 712.

mcq.s: The 'Chachnama', the account of the Arab conquest of Sindh, was translated into Persian by:
o: Muhammad Ali bin Abu Bakr Kufi
mcq.x: The Arabic Chachnama, the history of the Arab conquest of Sindh, was rendered into Persian by Muhammad Ali bin Abu Bakr Kufi in the 13th century.

mcq.s: Firdausi, the author of the Shahnama, was associated with the court of:
mcq.x: Firdausi, called the 'Homer of the East', wrote the Persian epic Shahnama and was a poet at the court of Mahmud of Ghazni.
